# Results — Study 460 (Counterattack / Meeting Lines)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
bullish counterattack (meeting) line reverses a downtrend: two opposite-colour candles whose
closes meet after a sell-off mark a bottom** — encoded as a mechanical rule. The pattern is a
down leg (close[t-1] < close[t-10]), a black candle at t-1, a white candle at t that gaps down
on the open and closes within 15 bps of the prior close (the "meeting"); a long fires on the
meeting bar's close, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the
forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **280** mechanical bullish meeting lines pooled across the 5 tapes (tol = 15 bps, trend_lookback = 10) |
| Timing / costs | down-leg + opposite-colour + gap + equal close read on bar *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per signal |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument pattern study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only
> the drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — meeting line vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch meeting-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = meeting − random.

| horizon | n | meeting | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (meet−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 280 | −7.6 bps  | 53% | −0.46 | +61.0 bps | **−68.6 bps** | −9.6 bps  | −3.01 | 0.003 |
| 10-day | 280 | +11.5 bps | 55% | +0.53 | +73.0 bps | **−61.5 bps** | +9.5 bps  | −1.97 | 0.049 |
| 20-day | 279 | +111.3 bps | 63% | +3.50 | +97.9 bps | **+13.4 bps** | +109.3 bps | +0.33 | 0.741 |
| 60-day | 278 | +264.6 bps | 70% | +4.20 | +118.0 bps | **+146.6 bps** | +262.6 bps | +1.99 | 0.047 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks respectable at the longer holds
(**+3.50** at 20 days, **+4.20** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an
upward-drifting index inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the
meeting line is *significantly worse* at the short holds where the pattern is supposed to act
(Δ = −68.6 bps at 5 days, Welch *t* = **−3.01**; −61.5 bps at 10 days). It only pulls ahead at
20–60 days — long after any "reversal" — and even there the meeting-minus-random difference
**never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max Welch *t* = +1.99 at 60 days, *p* = 0.047, on the
wrong side of the line). The pattern does not forecast the bounce it claims.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent cross-sectional edge

| ticker | entries | meeting | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (meet−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 51 | +41.1 bps | +0.71 | +36.7 bps | **+4.4 bps** |
| QQQ | 53 | +193.6 bps | +2.19 | +129.9 bps | **+63.7 bps** |
| IWM | 47 | +192.3 bps | +3.03 | +51.5 bps | **+140.8 bps** |
| DIA | 53 | +53.5 bps | +0.72 | +38.1 bps | **+15.4 bps** |
| GLD | 76 | +90.8 bps | +1.57 | +189.4 bps | **−98.7 bps** |

The 20-day delta is positive in 4 of 5 names, but the whole effect rides on **IWM** (+140.8 bps
on just 47 signals — small-cap noise) while **GLD** is −98.7 bps behind random. With ~50 signals
per name the per-ticker *t*'s are wide; this is the scattershot pattern of relabelled drift, not
a robust edge.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the meeting, nothing changes

The decisive "does the *equal close* matter?" test: keep the down-leg + opposite-colour +
gap-down context (the "almost-meeting" candidates) but **ignore the equal-close test**, drawing
the same number of entries at random from that candidate pool. If price genuinely respected the
*meeting* (not just a dip-buy after a down leg), the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed meeting 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY close-scramble placebo | +41.1 bps | **0.623** | 500 |

**62% of context-matched, no-meeting draws match or beat the real meeting line** (*p* = 0.623).
The equal close carries no information — any down-leg + gap-down candidate does just as well. The
"meeting forecasts the reversal" claim is busted; what little there is, is the down-leg dip-buy
(which is itself just drift, per the random baseline above).

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* meeting-line bounce (knob `edge`), the same rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | meeting | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 68 | −34.4 bps | 46% | −0.64 |
| **0.60** (real planted bounce) | 50 | +595.9 bps | 92% | **+9.86** |

With no planted bounce the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted bounce
lights up at *t* = +9.86 with a 92% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The bullish meeting line does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (meeting − random = −68.6 / −61.5 / +13.4 / +146.6 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the
  meeting-vs-random Welch *t* never clears 2 — it is **negative and significant** at the short
  holds (−3.01 at 5d) where the reversal is claimed, and only +1.99 at 60 days, *p* = 0.047).
  The respectable one-sample *t*'s (20-day +3.50, 60-day +4.20) are pure beta.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed; at the short horizon the pattern is *worse* than random, and costs only deepen the
  hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply by holding the index.
- **"Does the equal-close meeting forecast?" — BUSTED.** The close-scramble placebo leaves the
  result intact (*p* = 0.623): context-matched draws that ignore the meeting do as well as the
  real ones, so the defining equal close carries no forecasting information. The counterattack
  line is a descriptive label for a down-leg candle, not a forecasting signal.
